pr_body:
Today when setting up for the desired balance computation we move all shards to their desired locations without checking any allocation rules. However, certain allocation rules (e.g. those related to node versions and shutdowns) may prevent these movements in reality, resulting in a shard which cannot move to its desired location but which may not remain on its current node either.

This commit adds some checks to verify that these preliminary moves are still legal when setting up the computation.

Closes #93271

It seems the primary shard was allocated on the node that was upgraded. In such case the test executes `cancel shard`, however the shard was still allocated on the same node after the command was executed.

This seems to be a bug in the desired balance computation:

Steps to reproduce:

* Set up a cluster
```
node-0, 8.7.0 with primary shard [snapshot_based_recovery][0]
node-1, 8.6.0
```
* Set the allocation exclude for the index for the node-0 , however the index can not be moved as the other node is older
* Cancel the shard

Expected result: shard is started on the older `node-1`
Actual result: 
Desired balance computation re-assing the shard to exactly the same node using below code: [https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a2caf316fc634714f097afaaeea1c05c272c[…]luster/routing/allocation/allocator/DesiredBalanceComputer.java](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a2caf316fc634714f097afaaeea1c05c272ccf9a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/routing/allocation/allocator/DesiredBalanceComputer.java#L112-L114)
[https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a2caf316fc634714f097afaaeea1c05c272c[…]luster/routing/allocation/allocator/DesiredBalanceComputer.java](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a2caf316fc634714f097afaaeea1c05c272ccf9a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/routing/allocation/allocator/DesiredBalanceComputer.java#L143-L149)
